value.overview: The Torrent Tyrannulet (Serpophaga cinerea) is a small, active flycatcher closely associated with mountain streams. It perches on rocks, branches, and streamside vegetation before making short flights to catch insects. Its distinctive habitat, frequent tail-wagging, and preference for clear, fast-flowing water help separate it from other small tyrant flycatchers. The species has a discontinuous distribution in Central and South America, including Costa Rica, Panama, the Andes, and parts of Venezuela and Bolivia.
value.classification: The Torrent Tyrannulet belongs to the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae and the genus Serpophaga. Two subspecies are generally recognized, including the Central American form S. c. grisea.
value.identification: This is a small, slim tyrannulet measuring about 9.5 centimeters long. Adults are gray overall, with darker wings and tail, a whitish throat and underparts, and a dark head that may show a partly concealed pale crown patch. The bill is short and the tail is relatively long. It is often recognized more readily by behavior and habitat than by plumage: it repeatedly wags or flicks its tail while perched beside rocky watercourses and makes quick sallies after flying insects.
value.rangeHabitat: The Torrent Tyrannulet has a disjunct range. In Central America, the subspecies S. c. grisea occurs from the Cordillera de Tilarán in Costa Rica south through western Panama. In Costa Rica it is found mainly along rocky, fast-flowing mountain streams, especially at middle and upper elevations, generally around 500 meters and higher, although it can occur lower in some Caribbean-slope valleys. It uses forested stream margins, open riparian areas, and occasionally altered waterways or marshy habitats.
value.migrationStatus: It is considered a year-round resident rather than a long-distance migrant. In Costa Rica, individuals remain in suitable stream habitat throughout the year, with breeding records mainly from January through June. Local movements may occur when stream conditions or human activity alter habitat, but regular seasonal departure from Costa Rica is not established.
value.breeding: Breeding has been recorded in Costa Rica mainly from January through June. The nest is a small cup made from plant fibers and other vegetation, often covered externally with moss and lined with soft down. It is typically attached to streamside vegetation, frequently on a branch overhanging the water, usually less than a meter above the stream. Most documented nests have come from Costa Rica, where the species breeds along suitable mountain waterways.
value.dietFeeding: The Torrent Tyrannulet feeds mainly on arthropods, especially flying insects. It usually forages alone or in pairs from rocks, low branches, and vegetation beside streams. From a perch, it makes short flights to hawk insects in the air, then returns to the same or a nearby perch. It may also take prey from streamside foliage while hovering briefly and occasionally searches for food on gravel, paths, or other open ground.
value.behavior: This species is energetic and strongly tied to running water. It spends much of its time near boulders and low vegetation along streams, often perching in exposed positions where it can watch for insects. Repeated tail-wagging and tail-flicking are characteristic. It may occur singly or in pairs and commonly makes short, direct flights across the water. Its dependence on noisy mountain streams can make its calls difficult to detect, even when the bird is nearby.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population is not considered to be undergoing a major decline, although its specialized streamside habitat may make local populations sensitive to habitat degradation.
